subject: Information Theory
title: Patents and Knowledge Disclosure
description: A quick, practical guide to Patents and Knowledge Disclosure.

hook.text: A patent gives 20 years of monopoly. In exchange, you must publish exactly how your invention works. It's a deal.

buildup.text: The patent system trades temporary exclusivity for public disclosure. After 20 years, the information is free for all.

discovery.text: Without patents, inventors keep secrets forever. The system maximizes long-term info flow via short-term limits.

twist.text: Patent thickets—overlapping patents on similar ideas—can block innovation instead of promoting it. The system's flaw.

climax.text: In information theory, patents are a rate-distortion tradeoff. Restrict now to maximize total info released over time.

punchline.text: Reveal everything, control it temporarily. Patents trade time for truth.

quiz.question: What do inventors exchange for patent protection?
options: Full public disclosure of how the invention works
